data.title: Hua Medicine Announces Positive Topline Results from U.S. Phase 1b Multiple Ascending Dose Trial of Once-Daily HMS1005
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov 23, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - Hua Medicine (HKEX stock code: 2552) today announced positive topline results from its U.S. Phase 1b multiple ascending dose (MAD) trial of HMS1005, a second-generation glucokinase activator (GKA). The trial enrolled a heterogeneous population of adults (83% White) with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) in the United States. HMS1005 was generally well tolerated across multiple once-daily dose levels. Serum glucose measurements and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed improvements in glucose control over the 14-day treatment period.

Dorzagliatin, the world's first GKA, launched in 2022. More than 10 million packs have been used in China to treat T2D patients. Dorzagliatin is designed to restore glucose homeostasis by improving glucose sensing, pancreatic secretory function, GLP-1 secretion and hepatic glucose metabolism. This mechanism, together with the potential for disease modification and drug-free remission, informed the development of a second-generation, once-daily GKA for diabetes and other conditions associated with impaired glucose homeostasis and bioenergy deficiency.

HMS1005 is a second-generation glucokinase allosteric activator and a prodrug of dorzagliatin (HMS5552). Unlike dorzagliatin, which is taken twice daily, HMS1005 is designed for once-daily dosing. The Phase 1b study builds on Phase 1a pharmacokinetic findings, which showed efficient conversion of HMS1005 to dorzagliatin and prolonged systemic exposure.

The Phase 1b study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of HMS1005 in patients with Type 2 diabetes. The study enrolled 48 patients across six cohorts and evaluated once-daily doses ranging from 123 mg to 492 mg. The safety, tolerability, and HMS5552 exposure findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily oral therapy for Type 2 diabetes and related metabolic diseases worldwide.

Key Results

- Pharmacokinetics: HMS1005 was efficiently converted to dorzagliatin (HMS5552) across all once-daily dose groups (123 to 492 mg). The once-daily extended-release formulation showed a favorable dose-exposure profile for dorzagliatin based on peak concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), compared with findings from a prior MAD study of twice-daily dorzagliatin. These findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 in Phase 2 trials.

- Safety and tolerability: HMS1005 was generally safe and well tolerated at doses up to 492 mg once daily. No serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and no clinically meaningful hypoglycemia (blood glucose below 54 mg/dL or 3.0 mmol/L) was observed. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed no increase in time below range (TBR) at once-daily doses of 123 mg to 369 mg. 369 mg was identified as the maximum tolerated dose.

- Glycemic control: Continuous glucose monitoring showed improvements in glucose management indicator (GMI, an analogous measurement of blood glucose levels to HbA1c) and time in range (TIR). Across the drug tolerant once-daily dose groups from 123 mg to 369 mg, the TIR increased and GMI decreased with active parent drug HMS5552 exposure. The largest observed reduction in GMI was 1.48% in the cohort with high impaired beta-cell function, consistent with observations from dorzagliatin studies. The highest observed TIR increased from approximately 35% at baseline to more than 80% after treatment.

Advantage for once-daily prodrug PK profiles: The pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily extended-release oral therapy. The prodrug HMS1005 and active parent drug HMS5552 exposure profiles support a waiver of long-term GLP toxicity study in the HMS1005 clinical development. If confirmed by the regulatory agency, once-daily dosing second generation GKA development will be greatly accelerated.

Clinical Experience with Dorzagliatin

HMS1005 builds on Hua Medicine's experience with glucokinase activators. Dorzagliatin, marketed in mainland China as HuaTangNing , has demonstrated glucose-lowering efficacy and a favorable safety profile in previous clinical studies and post-marketing use. HuaTangNing has been prescribed to over 600,000 patients in mainland China.

At the 2026 American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions, Hua Medicine presented findings on dorzagliatin from HMM0601, a multicenter post-marketing real-world study involving 2,024 patients with Type 2 diabetes across 80 clinical centers. During the 52-week observation period, no drug-related serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and the incidence of clinically meaningful hypoglycemia was below 1%. Patients also demonstrated improvements in HbA1c and glycemic control.

At the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes Annual Meeting, further findings from HMM0601 showed that efficacy and safety of dorzagliatin in older adults (aged 65 years or older) and patients with reduced renal function were consistent with those observed in the overall study population.

Interim findings from HMM0701, a prospective real-world observational study, suggested that glucokinase activation may improve TIR and glucose homeostasis in patients with longstanding Type 2 diabetes.

A fixed-dose combination of dorzagliatin and metformin met its pivotal bioequivalence endpoints in recent clinical trials in mainland China. Hua Medicine expects to file a new drug application in 2027.

The clinical experience with dorzagliatin informs the development of HMS1005. Larger, longer trials are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of HMS1005 independently.

Next Steps

Hua Medicine plans to combine data from the Phase 1a and Phase 1b studies with existing clinical and nonclinical data for dorzagliatin to inform discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the HMS1005 development program. Future studies are expected to assess the efficacy and safety of selected once-daily doses over longer treatment periods, including effects on HbA1c and other measures of glycemic control.

Dr. Li Chen, Founder and CEO of Hua Medicine, said, 'The Phase 1b results support further development of HMS1005 and build on our experience with glucokinase activators.'

'Drawing on our clinical experience with dorzagliatin, we will continue to evaluate whether HMS1005 can improve glucose control with once-daily dosing. We also plan to explore its potential in other indications, including diabetes prevention, prediabetes, and mild cognitive impairment.'

Hua Medicine retains all global rights to HMS1005 and plans to engage with potential strategic and financial partners for development outside China.

About Type 2 Diabetes and Glucokinase

According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition), approximately 589 million adults worldwide are living with diabetes, a number projected to rise to 853 million by 2050. Type 2 diabetes accounts for the vast majority of cases. Despite the range of available therapies, many patients do not reach or maintain their blood glucose targets, as the disease progressively erodes the body's ability to sense and respond to changes in blood glucose.

Glucokinase (GK) serves as the body's glucose sensor. Found in the pancreas, liver and gut, it regulates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, hepatic glucose uptake and storage, and the release of incretin hormones such as GLP-1. Impaired glucokinase function is a key defect in T2D. Glucokinase activators (GKAs) are designed to restore this sensing function, addressing an underlying cause of the disease rather than only lowering blood glucose. Hua Medicine's dorzagliatin, approved in China in 2022, is the world's first approved GKA.

About HMS1005

HMS1005 is an investigational new molecular entity and a prodrug of dorzagliatin. It has global patent protection extending to at least 2042. Hua Medicine is developing an extended-release formulation for once-daily oral dosing, with the goal of sustaining glucose control and potentially improving treatment adherence.

About Hua Medicine

Hua Medicine (the 'Company') develops and commercializes drugs and is based in Shanghai, China, with companies in the United States and Hong Kong. Hua Medicine works with international partners to develop therapies for unmet medical needs, with a focus on diabetes. Hua Medicine's HuaTangNing ( dorzagliatin tablets) targets the glucose sensor glucokinase, restores glucose sensitivity in patients with Type 2 diabetes, and stabilizes imbalances in blood glucose levels in patients. HuaTangNing was approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China on September 30, 2022. It can be used alone or in combination with metformin for adult patients with Type 2 diabetes. For patients with chronic kidney disease, no dose adjustment is required. It is an oral glucose-lowering drug that can be used in T2D patients with renal function impairment.

In February 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS,was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Service of the Department of Health of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

In June 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS,was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Administration Bureau of the Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

Based on the International Diabetes Federation's 2025 Diabetes Atlas - 11th Edition, there are approximately 148 million diabetic patients in mainland China, 706,000 diabetic patients in Hong Kong SAR, and 52,000 diabetic patients in Macao SAR as of 2024.

data.title: The wind has finally shown up in Germany, and fossil fuels feel it: Maguire
data.description:
By Gavin Maguire

Germany's power market has spent much of this autumn waiting for the wind to return. That wait might be over.

Over the first three weeks of this month, wind generation surged from less than 100 gigawatt hours (GWh) to more than 1,100 GWh, lifting wind's share of total electricity production from just 6% to 65%, according to data from Germany's federal network agency.

As turbines across Germany spun back to life, coal and gas-fired generators rapidly surrendered market share, triggering one of the sharpest shifts in the country's generation mix this year.

The swing underscores a central reality of Europe's energy transition: when renewable output arrives at scale, fossil fuel demand can retreat with remarkable speed.

FROM WIND DROUGHT TO SURPLUS

The first half of November highlighted Germany's dependence on weather conditions.

Between November 8 and 10, wind generation averaged under 92 GWh and supplied less than 10% of total power output. During that period, fossil fuel generation climbed above 800 GWh a day and peaked at more than 910 GWh on November 10.

Gas plants carried much of the burden, generating nearly 418 GWh on November 10 alone, while output from lignite plants exceeded 316 GWh and hard coal generation approached 130 GWh.

The picture changed dramatically only a few days later.

By November 13, total wind output had climbed above 790 GWh. Two days later it reached nearly 736 GWh and supplied 56% of all electricity generation. On November 18, wind production exceeded 1,100 GWh and accounted for almost two-thirds of total generation.

Clean electricity output climbed in lockstep, reaching more than 1.3 terawatt hours (TWh) on November 18, the highest level in the period.

COAL TAKES THE BIGGEST HIT

The largest casualty of the wind rebound was coal generation.

Hard coal output fell from more than 136 GWh on November 11 to just 43 GWh by November 15. Lignite generation dropped from over 316 GWh on November 10 to below 149 GWh by November 18.

That pattern highlights how exposed coal generation has become to swings in renewable output. As wind production rises, coal is increasingly the first major source of supply to be displaced, making it the biggest loser in periods of strong renewable generation.

Germany's coal fleet remains crucial during periods of weak renewable generation. But the latest data show how quickly those plants can move from indispensable suppliers to secondary contributors when wind conditions improve.

GAS REMAINS THE SHOCK ABSORBER

Natural gas generation also retreated sharply as wind output climbed.

Gas-fired production fell from more than 417 GWh on November 10 to just 106 GWh on November 15, a decline of roughly three quarters in just five days.

Unlike coal, however, gas continues to serve a distinctive role within the system.

Gas units can ramp up and down far faster than coal plants, making them well suited to filling supply gaps when wind production fades and stepping back when renewable output surges.

The latest swings in generation demonstrate that flexibility has become one of the most valuable attributes in Europe's power market.

As renewable penetration rises, the ability to respond quickly matters as much as the ability to generate large volumes of electricity.

THE TAKEAWAY

The most important lesson from Germany's latest power data is not that wind generation has reached exceptional levels.

It is that fossil fuel demand has become increasingly dependent on weather conditions as renewable capacity expands. Once strong wind conditions emerge across Northern Europe, the resulting surge in renewable generation can erase vast amounts of coal and gas demand within days.

Within little more than a week, Germany moved from a system where fossil fuels supplied nearly three quarters of electricity generation to one where clean power dominated the mix and wind alone provided most of the country's electricity.

That is a glimpse of the direction of travel for Europe's broader power sector.

Each addition of wind and solar capacity increases the frequency and scale of periods when renewable generation displaces fossil fuels from the power mix.

Thermal power stations remain essential for reliability, but they are increasingly shifting from providers of routine electricity supply to providers of backup power during periods when renewable output falls short.

BLOWN AWAY

Only a week or so ago, traders were fixated on Germany's lack of wind and the pressure it was placing on power prices and fuel consumption.

Now the opposite challenge has emerged, as the return of strong winds has rapidly cut fossil fuel burn, squeezed coal generation and reduced the call on gas-fired power stations.

Power forecasters at LSEG are currently calling for German wind power generation to remain close to or above the long-term average for the next several weeks, which marks a sharp turnaround from early November forecasts that pegged wind generation at well below normal.

That reversal serves as a reminder that Europe increasingly operates two power systems at once: one determined by underlying electricity demand, and another determined by the weather.

When wind speeds collapse, coal and gas generation can surge within hours. When strong winds return, those same fossil-fuel plants can rapidly lose market share regardless of fuel prices or broader economic conditions.

For utilities, fuel suppliers and traders alike, that means weather forecasting is becoming ever more important in determining fossil fuel demand.

Germany's latest experience shows that as renewable capacity expands, the largest swings in coal and gas consumption may be driven not by policy decisions or geopolitical events, but by changing weather patterns across Europe's wind belts.

data.title: German automakers face winter of discontent as union battles loom
data.description:
Key points:
  • German auto workers earn about €65 hourly, data shows
  • Volkswagen faces IG Metall crunch talks on Tuesday, union threatens strikes from January 1
  • Germany's auto sector employment falls to lowest level in at least 21 years

By Christoph Steitz and Nick Carey

Germany's automakers face months of contentious labour talks and strikes over job cuts and potential factory closures as the model that underpinned the country's highly paid auto workforce breaks down.

For years, strong earnings from global markets helped offset Germany's high labour and production costs, analysts say. But Chinese competition, US tariffs and weaker demand are undermining the profits that made that possible.

Volkswagen , Mercedes-Benz , Bosch (ROBG.UL) and Schaeffler have responded with plans to cut thousands of jobs, curb investment and potentially close plants, moves likely to trigger fierce resistance from workers.

Andrew Bergbaum, a partner at consultancy AlixPartners, said declining investment returns and profitability point to a "difficult winter" in labour negotiations.

Volkswagen last month posted its biggest operating loss in more than a decade, while Mercedes-Benz and BMW saw their nine-month auto profit margins drop to 1.9% and 3.5%, respectively, down from 14.9% and 8.7% four years ago.

"They (unions) are in a very difficult place because companies aren't making any money, they're not investing any money, and management are increasingly bullish on trying to push through change," Bergbaum said.

FOCUS ON VOLKSWAGEN AND IG METALL TALKS

The tensions are most visible at Volkswagen, Europe's biggest automaker, which starts crunch talks on Tuesday with IG Metall, Germany's largest union, over fresh job and salary cuts. IG Metall has vowed fierce resistance to the company's demands.

Thorsten Groeger, the union's chief negotiator for wage talks with the company, said it was "out of the question" that an agreement could be reached this year as Volkswagen's offer was an insult to workers.

At €65 ($71) an hour, German auto workers are the world's highest paid, earning over one-and-a-half times more than their US counterparts and more than three times as much as workers in Poland, according to the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.

Volkswagen has said deep cost cuts are needed to remain competitive.

It aims to finalise a plan for its European factories by the end of June 2027, including a roadmap for four German sites the automaker says have no planned successor vehicle models.

The sites could be repurposed for military use, assigned vehicles for the Chinese market, or — failing other options — closed in the next decade, the company has said.

IG Metall has threatened strikes at Volkswagen from January 1 if no agreement is reached. One-day strikes have already hit BMW and Volkswagen's Audi division.

"We have to make sure we overcome the current tsunami in the sector and that companies do not go insolvent in the medium term. The IG Metall (union) must know this, too," said Daniel Bauer, head of Germany's SdK investor protection association.

The pressure extends beyond automakers. Europe's automotive suppliers will, on average, see their operating margins dwindle to 2.9% this year, down from 7.1% in 2018, a steeper fall than the decline to 5.8% from 9.0% at Chinese rivals, according to research from Roland Berger and Lazard.

"This is not just another downturn for European suppliers," said Roland Berger partner Felix Mogge. "Another round of cost cutting is simply not enough."

The industry's difficulties are also reflected in German jobs data.

Germany's auto sector workforce has fallen to the lowest level in at least 21 years, according to the federal statistics office.

"The fact is for Germany's car industry, there are going to be more job losses or fewer jobs created, however you look at it," said Ian Henry of consultancy AutoAnalysis.

DEEPER RESTRUCTURING AHEAD

Tesla's announcement last week of a €3 billion expansion of its plant near Berlin, four days after Mercedes-Benz said it would suspend German investments, underscored the contrast between established automakers and newcomers.

German automakers are producing fewer vehicles at home as overseas sales decline. Foreign sales fell nearly 8% between 2023 and 2025, according to data from industry lobby group VDA and the German statistics office.

Marco Santino, partner at management consultancy Oliver Wyman, said further cuts were likely, with automakers targeting more structural solutions and "not just these progressive layoffs that are going to reduce capacity, but probably not really solve the problem".

($1 = 0.9121 euros)

data.title: Citi's $35-billion UK error could complicate exit from US regulatory penalty box
data.description:
Key points:
  • Error exceeds 20% of risk-weighted assets at UK trading unit, Reuters calculations show
  • Morningstar says issue could lengthen sustained-effectiveness test but likely would not reset consent-order process
  • Citi says unit stayed above regulatory minimums with no impact on holding company or main bank

By Stephen Gandel and Saeed Azhar

An error that caused Citigroup to underestimate its risk-weighted assets by $35 billion, forcing it to inject capital into a UK unit, could complicate a long-running effort to exit a US regulatory penalty that has been a drag on its operations, experts said.

While the misstatement happened in an overseas unit, it could raise questions for US regulators over whether Citi's penalties, or consent orders, from the regulators should be speedily lifted, said some analysts and former regulators.

The orders cover regulatory demands to fix risk management, data governance and other problems and they date back to 2020, leading to costly fines and distractions for Citi. Reuters was first to report the $35-billion error on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

"It’s not a huge error given the size of the bank, but any misstep is going to complicate their efforts to escape their consent order," said Sheila Bair, a former head of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. "As a general matter, I think this just reinforces the unreliability of models in setting risk-based capital requirements."

While the error could complicate reaching the goal, it is unlikely to completely derail the bank getting the consent orders lifted, some analysts said.

Citi Chief Executive Jane Fraser has said that exiting the consent order was her top priority, and she appeared to be nearing that goal.

Last month, Reuters reported that as recently as this summer, the bank was targeting the end of this year, or the first quarter, to submit the needed paperwork to regulators that could lead to the bank being able to conclude its remediation efforts, which have forced the bank to hire tens of thousands of additional employees.

HIGHER BAR

The third-largest US bank has been aiming to present a comprehensive audit to the Federal Reserve and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, so it will not hit any delays in approval, Reuters previously reported.

"With the event in question occurring during a time period that overlaps with Citi's own attestation work regarding remediation efforts to lift the consent order, it could plausibly lengthen the duration for the 'sustained effectiveness' test, but it would be unlikely to reset the process," said Austin Taggart, a banking analyst at Morningstar.

As part of the consent order, regulators have ordered Citi to attest that data that it uses to file its required regulatory disclosures is correct and will be in the future.

Wells Fargo analysts led by Mike Mayo said in a note to clients that the mistake was not material from a regulatory perspective but that Citi suffered from having made mistakes in its past.

"The perception is not great since the bar is higher for Citi after its prior mistakes," Mayo said.

Citigroup said on Thursday it ​had identified and resolved an internal capital modeling issue at a European trading subsidiary this summer. "The subsidiary remained fully compliant with regulatory minimums throughout, with no impact on ​the holding company or main operating bank," it said.

On Friday, Citi declined to comment on any potential impact on prospects for its consent order.

On the question of whether this would create a setback for Citi resolving its consent order, the Federal Reserve declined to comment. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency did not return a request for comment.

REGULATORY HEARTBURN

While small in relation to Citi's firm-wide financials, the misstatement was more than 20% of the total risk-weighted assets in Citigroup Global Markets Ltd (CGML), the UK-based international brokerage operation where the error occurred, which had $155 billion as of the end of 2025, according to Reuters calculations based on regulatory filings.

Risk-weighted assets are central to regulatory reporting, because they determine how much capital a bank has to hold in order to absorb losses. At issue is how and when banks use internal models to measure risk or standardized models developed by regulators. In many cases, banks need approval from regulators to use internal models.

The UK unit used an internal model to determine the riskiness of assets that had not been approved by regulators for some trades, people familiar with the matter have told Reuters. When the error emerged and the trades were plugged into the correct model, the measure of risk the unit was taking shot up and Citi was not holding enough loss-absorbing capital, they said.

Some experts said that even though the error happened in the UK, it will still be a concern in Washington.

"The first order of this is that it is a UK problem, but Citi is a US holding company so I would expect this issue to be reflected in the Federal Reserve's oversight of the US holding company," said Jeremy Kress, an associate professor of business law and a former Fed regulatory attorney.

"The first order is that this is a big screw-up, but the second order is that if they are screwing that up, what else are they missing, which is what will really give regulators heartburn."

data.title: NFLX Vs DIS: Which Streaming Stock Is A Favorite Among Analysts?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Phillip Securities downgraded Disney to ‘Accumulate’ from ‘Buy’ with an unchanged price target of $130 following its fourth-quarter earnings report.
  • Morningstar said in a note that it believes that the negative sentiment around NFLX stock has created “the best buying opportunity for Netflix shares in years.” 
  • On Stocktwits, retail messages around NFLX stock climbed 73% over 24 hours, while message volume around DIS stock jumped 340% in the same time. 

Streaming stocks Netflix Inc. (NFLX) and Walt Disney Co. (DIS) have been garnering retail attention amid their latest earnings releases and Wall Street chatter.

On Stocktwits, retail messages around NFLX stock climbed 73% over 24 hours, according to platform data, while message volume around DIS stock jumped 340% in the same period.

Phillip Securities downgraded Disney’s stock over the weekend, according to The Fly, while Morningstar also released a fresh take on Netflix, maintaining its $80 price target.

Disney Stock Slips Most In Nearly 2 Months 

DIS stock slipped 1.89% on Friday, marking its steepest decline since Oct. 1, amid broader market weakness following constrained liquidity due to Anthropic’s (ANT) IPO.

Meanwhile, Phillip Securities downgraded Disney to ‘Accumulate’ from ‘Buy’ with an unchanged price target of $130 following its fourth-quarter earnings report. The firm cited valuation concerns for the downgrade, adding that it believes Disney remains well-positioned to deliver sustainable long-term earnings growth.

Disney Q4 Earnings Snapshot

Last week, Disney reported its Q4 results, reporting revenue of $25.95 billion, up 16% year-over-year and beating Wall Street estimates. Diluted earnings per share came in at $1.51, more than double the $0.73 reported in the comparable quarter of 2025.

For the full year, revenue reached about $102.3 billion, up roughly 8% year-over-year, and full-year adjusted EPS rose to $7.02, about 18% higher than in 2025.

Disney projected double-digit adjusted EPS growth and an 8% increase in segment operating income, with high-single-digit growth across Entertainment, Experiences, and Sports.

Netflix Tumbles To 52-Week Low

NFLX stock tumbled to a 52-week low of $56.56 on Friday as slowing revenue growth, downgraded advertising expectations, rising competitive pressures, and potentially high-cost bidding for major live events ratcheted up selling pressure.

Netflix reported its Q3 2026 financial results on Oct. 20, 2026, delivering revenue of $12.87 billion, an 11.9% year-over-year increase and matching analyst expectations. Meanwhile, EPS came in at $0.87, beating Wall Street consensus estimates.

The streaming giant projected the following quarter’s revenue at $13.44 billion, slightly below analyst expectations.

However, Netflix's year-over-year revenue growth has gradually decelerated, dropping from about 17.6% in late 2025 to roughly 11.8% in the third quarter of 2026. Its fourth-quarter revenue growth projection is 11.5%.

Meanwhile, in its latest earnings report, management cut its 2026 advertising revenue forecast to roughly $2.7 billion, down from an earlier target of $3 billion, citing delays in ad-tech rollout and partner deals.

Morningstar Says ‘Being Too Bearish’ On Netflix Is A Mistake

Morningstar said in a report last week that while Netflix's Q3 results were good, management commentary reinforced growth fears. It also highlighted disappointing engagement and that advertising sales will likely fall short of the 2026 target.

However, the analyst believes that the negative sentiment has created “the best buying opportunity for Netflix shares in years,” adding that “many of its markets are mature and won't grow at the rate they did when they were rapidly adding new subscribers, but it still has growth drivers.”

Morningstar noted that the ad-supported tier will launch in 15 international markets in 2027, a catalyst that will likely drive a surge in new members, as initially happened in markets where the ad tier was originally offered. Management said customer churn declined from last year to better-than-anticipated levels in the U.S. and internationally.

“We expect additional US price increases in 2027 and further advertising growth, as Netflix better fills inventory and narrows the revenue gap between ad-supported and ad-free users,” it said.

The firm has an $80 fair value estimate and a narrow moat on NFLX stock. “A growth slowdown was inevitable, but Netflix remains far superior to its subscription streaming peers, and its valuation multiples are now very reasonable, as we still expect double-digit annual profit growth,” it said.

Wall Street Stance On NFLX, DIS Stocks

Based on Koyfin data, the 12-month average price target on NFLX stock is $84.55, implying a 49% upside. Of the 51 analysts covering the stock, 33 have a ‘Buy’ or higher rating on the stock, while 16 have a ‘Hold’ rating and the remaining two have a ‘Sell’ or lower rating on the stock.

Meanwhile, on Disney, the 12-month average price target is at $131.34, suggesting an upside of more than 11%. Of the 32 analysts covering the stock, 27 have a ‘Buy’ or higher rating on the stock, while four have a ‘Hold’ rating, and one has a ‘Sell’ rating.

NFLX, DIS Stocks: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around NFLX stock was ‘extremely bearish’ at the time of writing.

One user said, “$NFLX should be $49 after this week and that will be the end of that.” NFLX shares closed at $56.73 on Friday.

However, another user said, “$NFLX I cant believe there is bearish sentiment around this obvious of a buy.”

Meanwhile, retail sentiment around DIS stock was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing.

However, one user said, “$DIS The parks were their last life line and they are empty after destroying Splash Mountain and flushing their reputation down the toilet.”

NFLX stock is down more than 39% year-to-date, while DIS stock has gained about 4.5% in the same time.

data.title: Maybank Profit Climbs on Stronger Fee Income, Beating Estimates — Update
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

Malayan Banking posted stronger-than-expected net profit in the third quarter, driven by higher core fee income and net fund-based income.

Malaysia's largest lender by market capitalization said Monday that quarterly net profit rose 4.7% from a year earlier to 2.74 billion ringgit, equivalent to $666.2 million. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had expected 2.71 billion ringgit.

A 7.7% increase in core fees, led by higher wealth-management and investment banking-related income, supported the bottom line, Maybank said. Net fund-based income also grew, rising 2.3% to 5.12 billion ringgit as net interest margin improved five basis points to 2.07%.

However, net interest income--the difference between interest earned on loans and that paid on deposits--slipped 4.3% to 3.13 billion ringgit, and noninterest income fell 3.2% to 2.38 billion ringgit, it said.

Net impairment provisions for the quarter declined 39% to 215.2 million ringgit.

Maybank Chief Executive Khairussaleh Ramli said that while its diversified businesses and regional operations supported performance, the group remains cautious about the outlook amid global economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainty.

Shares of the Malaysian lender have declined nearly 5% this year, pressured by concerns about funding costs and net interest margins as bond yields rise amid a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook.

The planned expansion of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index to 50 constituents from 30, aimed at reducing the index's concentration in financial stocks, has also weighed on sentiment toward the bank, an index heavyweight.

Analysts said a potential rate hike by Malaysia's central bank next March could offer Malaysian banks some respite. Banks' net interest margins have been squeezed as U.S. Treasury yields lift domestic bond yields and funding costs and intense deposit competition pushes lenders to offer higher rates.

A 25-basis-point increase in Bank Negara Malaysia's policy rate could improve Maybank's net interest margin by 2.6 basis points, according to estimates by CIMB Securities, which is overweight on the Malaysia banking sector.

That relief would likely be temporary, however. The potential rate increase is a short-term positive catalyst for banks' margins rather than a structural solution to the sector's funding challenges, CIMB Securities analyst Ei Leen Tan said.

data.title: Gold, silver rebound over 2% on MCX: 3 key dates buyers should watch before purchasing
data.description:
Gold and silver prices rebounded on Monday, November 23, after suffering a sharp correction last week. While the decline has brought bullion prices to levels last seen more than a year ago, buyers may want to watch three key US developments before making fresh purchases.

On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures for December 4 delivery rose 2.53% to ₹1.24 lakh per 10 grams, while silver futures for the same expiry gained 2.44% to ₹1.51 lakh per kg.

The recovery follows an 11% fall in MCX gold and a 16.2% decline in silver last week.

However, the rebound does not necessarily mean the correction is over. The US inflation reading on November 25, employment data on December 4 and the Federal Reserve's policy decision on December 9 could influence the next move in precious metals.

Three dates that could determine the next move

November 25: US inflation data

The inflation reading will offer clues on whether price pressures in the US are easing. Higher-than-expected inflation could strengthen expectations of interest rates remaining elevated for longer, supporting the dollar and weighing on non-yielding assets such as gold and silver. Softer inflation could have the opposite effect.

December 4: US jobs data

The employment report will help investors assess the strength of the US economy. Strong jobs data could give the Federal Reserve more room to maintain higher interest rates, while signs of a weakening labour market could strengthen expectations of a less restrictive monetary policy.

December 9: US Federal Reserve decision

The Fed's policy announcement and commentary will be closely watched for signals on the interest rate trajectory. A hawkish stance could put renewed pressure on bullion, while indications of a softer policy outlook could support prices.

Should buyers wait before purchasing gold and silver?

Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus.com, said the latest recovery reflects a reassessment of the likelihood of further US interest rate increases, alongside a decline in US bond yields and the dollar.

However, he cautioned against treating the rebound as a reason to increase exposure to both metals equally. If expectations of fewer rate increases stem from weakening economic growth, gold could benefit from safe-haven demand, while silver could face concerns over industrial demand.

He said buyers accumulating gold for a known future expense could use the correction to secure part of their requirement.

Darshan Desai, CEO of Aspect Bullion & Refinery, said the correction has created buying opportunities, particularly for consumers planning wedding-related jewellery purchases.

However, he expects volatility to continue, with US inflation data, Fed signals and currency movements influencing prices. Consumers are likely to favour staggered purchases rather than committing to large volumes at once.

For buyers without an immediate requirement, tracking the three upcoming developments could provide greater clarity before making a substantial purchase.

Those with near-term jewellery needs could consider staggered buying instead of trying to time the market bottom.

data.title: Auto retail hits record 55.25 lakh units during 42-day festive season, EV sales surge 53%: FADA
data.description:
Automobile retail sales in India rose 2.21% year-on-year to a record 55.25 lakh units during the 42-day festive season this year, despite a high base following the GST 2.0-led demand surge last year, dealer body FADA said on Monday.

According to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), total vehicle retail sales stood at 55,25,490 units during the 42-day festive period of 2026, the highest-ever for the corresponding period.

Compared with the festive season of 2024, vehicle retail sales registered a growth of 23.95%, indicating sustained demand momentum following the GST rate rationalisation.

Two-wheeler retail sales grew 3.67% to 43,13,276 units, while three-wheeler sales rose 5.32% to 1,93,576 units.

Commercial vehicle retail sales increased 7.13 per cent to 1,55,761 units, tractor sales grew 2.24% to 1,03,809 units and construction equipment sales surged 26.06% to 10,452 units.

However, passenger vehicle retail sales declined 7.16% to 7,48,616 units against 8,06,322 units in the year-ago period.

The biggest highlight of the season was the surge in electric vehicle adoption, with EV retail sales jumping 52.62% to cross five lakh units for the first time during a single festive period, led by electric two-wheelers (61.10% rise) and electric passenger vehicles (up 72.91%), with electric commercial vehicles more than doubling.

Close to one in ten festive vehicles sold this season was electric, FADA stated.

FADA President Sai Giridhar said: "The 42-day festive season of 2026 will be remembered as the year Indian auto retail set a record on top of a record. Against last year's extraordinary base, which got amplified by GST 2.0, the twin festivals delivered an all-time high -- festive retails this year still grew 2.21 per cent to 55,25,490 units, the highest-ever 42-day festive season in our history."

Looking ahead, FADA said India was approaching a historic milestone of recording over 3 crore vehicle retail sales in a calendar year for the first time.

The festive season has set the stage for this achievement, it added.

data.title: Marksans Pharma shares fall 3% after USFDA flags six observations at Goa facility
data.description:
Shares of Marksans Pharma fell over 3% in intraday trading on Monday, November 23, extending losses for the second straight day after being issued a Form 483 by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The company said the USFDA issued a Form 483 containing six observations following a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) inspection at its manufacturing facility in L-82 and L-83, Verna Industrial Estate, Goa, according to an exchange filing on Monday.

The inspection was conducted from November 12 to November 20.

The company said all observations were procedural in nature, with none relating to data integrity or repeat findings. It added that it would work with the US FDA to address them within the stipulated timeline.

The observations were not expected to affect the site's new product pipeline or commercial supplies, according to the filing.

What are Current Good Manufacturing Practices?

Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMP) are minimum quality standards set by regulators such as the US FDA and the World Health Organisation (WHO) to ensure that medicines, food and certain biological products are consistently manufactured, processed, packaged and stored safely and meet quality requirements.

What is a Form 483?

A Form 483 lists observations made by US FDA inspectors during a facility inspection. It is shared with the company at the closing meeting but does not represent the FDA's final assessment of its compliance with manufacturing standards.

The company is generally given 15 days to respond, outlining how it plans to address the observations.

How has the market reacted

Marksans Pharma shares fell 3.13% as of 10.19 am on Monday, extending their decline to a second consecutive session. The stock had snapped a four-session losing streak on Thursday before falling again on Friday.

Despite the recent losses, the shares are up around 57% year-to-date and 47% over the past 12 months.

data.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $1.8 billion in past week as outflows become ‘structural’: analysts
data.description:
Spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds in the U.S. reported around $1.79 billion in net outflows last week, the largest weekly withdrawal since the week ended June 26, 2026.

This marked the fourth consecutive week of outflows for the funds, according to data from SoSoValue. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led the outflows with $1.37 billion alone during the week.

So far this month, around $4.14 billion has left bitcoin ETFs, trailing June's record monthly net outflows. Total net assets in the bitcoin ETFs sat at $71.35 billion as of Friday, down from around $110 billion in mid-September.

Spot ether (ETH) ETFs also reported $314 million in weekly outflows, making it the eighth consecutive week of negative flows.

Laevitas Head of Markets Rick Maeda told The Block that the current net outflow represents "mostly risk reduction" among investors. "Profit-taking usually follows a rally, but these outflows have come into a falling market, with BTC sliding from around $80,000 at the start of the month to the low $60,000s," said Maeda.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell to a cycle low near $55,700 over the weekend amid continued risk-off sentiment, macro headwinds, and an AI equities-led stock market downturn. The Nasdaq Composite fell around 10% last week, and the S&P 500 dropped 8.6% as the scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang fueled wider concerns about the sustainability of the AI sector. The Block's Bitcoin Fear and Greed Index currently shows 11 — extreme fear.

"Being on the far end of the risk asset spectrum, whilst also facing its own headwinds such as quantum computing and hacks, crypto has been an easy asset for investors to get rid of from their portfolios," Maeda added.

Structural outflows

Dan Khus, chief analyst at LVRG Research, said the current ETF outflow streak appears to be more structural than previous outflows.

"Unlike earlier outflow periods that were often shorter and more reactive to single events, the current four-week streak appears more structural, coinciding with sustained price pressure, elevated liquidations, and a shift in institutional positioning toward capital preservation," Khus commented.

Risk-averse investors are moving further away from crypto products as they expect the Federal Reserve to deliver another interest rate hike in December, analysts said. The U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index, scheduled to be announced this Wednesday, may hint at how sticky inflation remains, and whether the Federal Reserve will proceed with another rate hike in December, BTSE COO Jeff Mei said.

"Bitcoin and ether ETFs may face further outflows as rate-hike concerns and weak risk appetite weigh on institutional demand," Zeus Research Analyst Dominick John said. "Bitcoin is likely to remain more resilient, while Ether faces greater pressure. A sustained recovery will depend on easing macro fears and renewed inflows."

Most sectoral indices trade lower

TCS, Tech Mahindra among top two gainers

What’s the reason behind the optimism in Indian IT sector?

The rally in Indian IT stocks came even as Asian equity markets remained under pressure as investors sold AI stocks amid reports of some governments in the region taking measures to stop stock prices from crashing further. US curbs on chip exports to certain countries to restrict China’s access to its AI developments also weighed the region’s markets down. Rising interest rates also made investors cautious.

The latest sell-off in the Asian markets reflects growing concerns over stretched technology valuations, the scale and financing of AI-related capital expenditure, and uncertainty over the returns on these investments, said Dow Jones Newswires reported, citing Commerzbank analysts.

Several Asian governments have also taken steps to contain market volatility. China eased margin requirements for investors borrowing to buy stocks to 80 percent from 100 percent. data.title: Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services Reports Third Quarter and Nine- Month 2026 Financial Results; Achieves Record Quarterly Core Profit
data.description:
TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services, a leading Israeli insurance and financial group (), ("Harel Insurance Investments", "the Group" or "the Company") today reported its third quarter and first nine months 2026 results.

Highlights:

  • Core profit in Q3 2026 surpassed NIS 1 billion for the first time, setting a new quarterly record and representing a 50% increase over the past two years. Growth was driven by continued increase in insurance underwriting profit, as well as higher profits from asset management and credit activities. Core profit in the first nine months peaked at NIS 2.8 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.7 billion).
  • Comprehensive income after tax in the first nine months was NIS 2.06 billion, (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.17 billion); ROE was 23%.
  • Comprehensive income after tax in Q3 2026 was NIS 477 million (Q3 2025: NIS 840 million), the decline in comprehensive income was due to negative nostro return; ROE was 16%.
  • Contractual Service Margin (CSM) from new sales in the first nine months of 2026 increased by 15% to NIS 1.45 billion, reflecting continuous growth in value creation in life and health insurance, which enhances future profitability. The CSM as of September 30, 2026, was NIS 17.9 billion, industry highest.
  • Total premiums, contributions and amounts received for investment contracts grew 16% to NIS 38.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, AUM increased to NIS 654 billion as of September 30, 2026, up 15% in the past twelve months.
  • The Company's Board of Directors declared a dividend of NIS 300 million. Year-to-date, total capital returned to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks amounted to approximately NIS 1.9 billion.
  • Harel Insurance's Solvency Capital Ratio increased to 176% as of June 30, 2026, from 165% as of December 31, 2025 (including transitional measures and the Tier 2 issuance).
  • Harel Insurance's outlook revised to Positive from Stable by S&P Global Ratings, which affirmed its 'A-' long-term issuer credit and financial strength ratings.

Business performance overview:

  • Core profit after tax in Q3 2026 increased by 8% to NIS 696 million (Q3 2025: NIS 647 million).
  • Core profit after tax in the first nine months of 2026 increased by 7% to NIS 1.9 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 1.8 billion).

Insurance:

  • Core profit before tax from insurance activity in Q3 2026 was NIS 792 million (Q3 2025: NIS 735 million). Core profit is calculated based on an assumed annual margin of 2% and excluding special effects.
  • Core profit before tax from insurance activity in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 2.12 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.09 billion). The increase was driven by higher core profits in life and health insurance, supported by increase in sales of growth products (life risks, medical expenses and critical illness), and was partially offset by lower core profit in non-life insurance.
  • The future value of new business (CSM new business) in the first nine months of 2026 amounted to NIS 1.45 billion, up 15% compared to the same period last year, reflecting significant value creation from the focus on growth products, which supports future profitability. Total CSM as of September 30, 2026, amounted to NIS 17.9 billion.

Asset management and credit:

  • Core profit from asset management in Q3 2026 increased 13% to NIS 120 million (Q3 2025: NIS 106 million), driven by continued growth in assets under management and management fees. The asset management segment, which includes pension and provident funds, mutual funds, ETFs and investment contracts, had assets under management of NIS 514 billion, as of September 30, 2026, an increase of NIS 79 billion in the past twelve months.
  • Core profit from the credit segment in Q3 2026 increased 11% to NIS 69 million (Q3 2025: NIS 62 million), reflecting ongoing growth in credit activity. The credit portfolio reached NIS 9.1 billion, as of September 30, 2026, an increase of NIS 2.3 billion in the past twelve months.

Overview of business segments performance

Health Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 550 million (Q3 2025: NIS 605 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 1.27 billion compared to NIS 1.16 billion in the same period last year.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 increased by 15% to NIS 373 million (Q3 2025: NIS 324 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 793 compared to NIS 807 million in the same period last year.

Life Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 2 million (Q3 2025: NIS 244 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 529 million compared to NIS 792 million in the same period last year. The decline in comprehensive income was driven by lower finance and investment income.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 increased 28% to NIS 226 million (Q3 2025: NIS 177 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 611 million compared to NIS 605 million in the same period last year.

Non-life Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 46 million (Q3 2025: NIS 278 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 645 million compared to NIS 858 million in the same period last year. The decline in comprehensive income reflects lower finance and investment income.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 was NIS 93 million (Q3 2025: NIS 113 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 344 million, an increase of NIS 18 million from NIS 326 million in the same period last year.

Asset management (Pension, Provident, Financial Services and Investment Contracts):

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax from pension and provident funds was NIS 59 million (Q3 2025: NIS 51 million). In the first nine months of the year, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 171 million compared to NIS 121 million in the same period last year. Results were affected by an increase in management fees driven by growth in AUM.
  • In Q3 2026 comprehensive income before tax from financial services (mutual funds, ETFs) and investment contracts was NIS 57 million (Q3 2025: NIS 51 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax from financial services (mutual funds, ETFs) and investment contracts was NIS 165 million, compared to NIS 119 million in the same period last year.
  • As of September 30, 2026, total assets under management in the asset management segment amounted to NIS 514 billion.

Credit:

  • In Q3 2026, core profit of the credit segment was NIS 69 million (Q3 2025: NIS 62 million). In the first nine months of 2026, core profit of the credit segment was NIS 209 million compared to NIS 169 million in the corresponding period last year. Profitability was supported by continued growth of the credit portfolio in development property financing, mortgages and credit to mid-sized businesses.
  • The credit portfolio amounted to NIS 9.1 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to NIS 6.8 billion as of September 30, 2025, an increase of NIS 2.3 billion.

Conference Call information

Harel Insurance Investments will hold a conference call for analysts and investors in Hebrew on November 23, 2026, at 1 pm (Israel); 11 am (UK); dial in details: https://www.veidan-conferencing.com/harel. On the same date, prior to the conference call, an investor presentation (including an English version) will be available on the Israel Securities Authority's reporting website (MAGNA), and on the Company's Investor Relations website: https://pr.harel-group.co.il/

This press release, the Investor presentation and the conference call for analysts and investors are not exhaustive and do not replace the Company's latest financial reports, which contain all relevant information including forward-looking statements, as defined in the Israeli securities Law, and set out in the aforementioned reports, and the need to review those financial reports in full.

For more information, please visit Harel's Investor Relations website or contact us at investor.relations@harel-ins.co.il

About Harel Insurance Investments

Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services Ltd. is a leading Israel-based insurance, financial services and asset management group, traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (). The company is Israeli largest insurer, engaged in health, life and non-life insurance, as well as in asset management – pension funds, provident funds and financial services such as mutual funds, ETFs and portfolio management, and credit activities. With assets under management of about NIS 654 billion, annual premiums and deposits inflows of NIS 45.7 billion and leading market shares across its business segments, Harel is well positioned to benefit the growing Israeli economy by leveraging its diversified business model, strong capital position, and long-standing expertise to deliver sustainable growth and resilient profitability. data.title: Citi Trims Ether Forecast by 6% — Market Talk
data.description:
0540 GMT - Citi cut its price target for ether to $2,838 from $3,028 as outflows from exchange-traded funds persist. Citi's Alex Saunders says ether ETFs have seen net outflows of roughly $4.5 billion since the beginning of October, while posting negative flows in each of the past seven weeks. "Total crypto market capitalization has fallen to the low end of its one-year range, and the sell-off hit ether hardest," Saunders says. Ether is 0.7% higher at $1,731.97. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

0529 GMT - Citi lowered its 12-month bitcoin forecast to $99,532 from $113,000 on lower exchange-traded fund demand and a tighter macroeconomic backdrop. Citi's Alex Saunders says ETF demand has deteriorated, as bitcoin slips back into year-to-date outflows. A stronger dollar, higher real yields and a spike in equity volatility were another reason why the bank cut its flows forecast from upside to neutral. "Capital appears to be leaving the ecosystem, leaving near-term direction tied to macro rather than crypto-specific catalysts," he writes. Bitcoin is 0.8% higher at $61,367. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

0421 GMT - Bitcoin edges higher in Asia after another punishing selloff over the weekend brought it to its lowest in over two years. The cryptocurrency's rebound shows that buyers were willing to return when the price fell to near $55,000, says Linh Tran at XS.com. But expectations of interest-rate hikes, a still-strong dollar and continued ETF outflows keep the outlook cautious. Over the next few sessions, Tran leans toward Bitcoin trading around $60,000. It will likely struggle to return to the $65,000 area anytime soon. If Bitcoin can hold above $60,000 through the U.S. sessions early this week--especially if ETFs are still seeing outflows--that would show that buying is strong enough to absorb the selling, Tran says. Bitcoin is up 0.6% at $61,236. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0412 GMT - The dollar is likely to trade around 160.00 yen throughout 2027, Morgan Stanley says in a note. Elevated Fed terminal-rate pricing and improving risk sentiment should support the dollar against the yen, while repeated verbal intervention by Japanese financial authorities should limit the yen's depreciation, the U.S. bank says. Japan's terms of trade are also expected to improve gradually next year, supporting the yen, Morgan Stanley says. A sustained downtrend in the dollar would require markets to price U.S. disinflation and a subsequent Fed easing cycle with greater conviction, the bank says. The dollar is at Y159.01. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

0408 GMT - The Bank of Korea is expected to hike rates on Thursday in a likely unanimous decision, says BofA Global Research in a report. With headline inflation running above 2.5%, the case for the BOK to consider further tightening to contain inflationary pressures remains strong. Korea's widening current account surplus continues to support the won, but persistent selling by foreign equity investors has weighed on the domestic market with the benchmark Kospi struggling to hold above 5000. The BOK's 2027 GDP growth forecast will be a key figure to watch. "An upgrade to above 3.5% would signal a more bullish assessment of the ongoing semiconductor upcycle and potentially point to greater risk of further rate hikes, implying a more hawkish policy stance than we currently expect," it adds. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)

0323 GMT - Singapore's industrial production growth likely moderated in October, reflecting high base effects, DBS economists say in a note. The city-state's output surged by 15% on year during the same period last year, marking its strongest monthly gain in 2025, they note.Robust artificial intelligence-related demand likely supported precision engineering and electronics production, although electronics growth may have moderated, the economists say. DBS expects Singapore's industrial production growth to slow to 1.0% in October from 3.4% in September. The data is due later this week.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0240 GMT - The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment spurred by regional equity-market weakness. There are "concerns over elevated interest rates, persistent inflation pressures and the unwinding of crowded AI-related positions," UOB Global Economics & Markets Research says in a report. Based on technical analysis, however, the U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair's upward momentum has faded following its recent pullback, two members of the research team note. The U.S. dollar has probably entered a range-trading phase between S$1.2885 and S$1.2915, they add. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 1.2898 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0229 GMT - Malaysia's exports could continue to remain resilient in 1Q 2027, supported by sustained AI-driven demand for electrical and electronic products and stronger energy shipments, says CGS International economist Mas Aida Che Mansor in a note. Global semiconductor sales are forecast to grow 29% in 2027. Domestic electrical and electronics capacity utilization of 87.7% also points to continued shipment growth despite rising base effects, she reckons. Petroleum and liquefied natural gas exports should provide additional support, driven by regional demand and resilient manufacturing activity in China and the Asean region. However, a sharper slowdown in the U.S. or China, weaker crude oil prices and rising trade protectionism could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0206 GMT - There are good reasons to believe that Australia's current housing market downturn is different to the garden variety cyclical downswings of recent decades, says Paul Bloxham, chief economist for Australia at HSBC. The decline so far is already bigger and sharper than the previous ones, while core inflation remains elevated, despite aggressive interest rate increases this year, he adds. Near-term interest rate cuts are not on the agenda while tax changes and the likelihood that global rates will stay high for longer are adding to the grim picture. Bloxham expects a 13% peak-to-trough house price fall. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0145 GMT - There could come a moment of acute discomfort for Australia money markets on Wednesday if inflation data for October delivers a higher-than-expected shock. Headline inflation is expected to rise to an uncomfortable 4.7%, but the more important trimmed mean measure is forecast to be little changed, landing at around 3.6% year over year. With recent economic data coming in weak, markets are already starting to price in interest-rate cuts next year, so an upward inflation shock would trigger volatility. Reserve Bank of Australia Gov. Michele Bullock said last week inflation risks remain skewed toward a rise. Central bank rhetoric remains hawkish generally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0125 GMT - The rates shock has likely evolved into a growth shock, two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a note. The "AI de-risking hits equities, EM carry and metals," the strategists say. Worries over the artificial-intelligence investment cycle have driven equities and U.S. yields lower, shifting the brunt of U.S. dollar strength toward emerging-market currencies, the strategists say. "In the near term, the USD should continue to benefit from hawkish Fed risks and the pressure that tighter global financial conditions place on the rest of the world," the strategists add. The U.S. Dollar Index is little changed at 103.763, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0108 GMT - Voters in Australia's southern state of Victoria are expected to hand the current Labor government a huge defeat at elections on Saturday. The mood is grim for the party, and if the drubbing is delivered, questions will be asked about what it means for the federal Labor government. It is likely to officially establish the right-wing populist One Nation party as a force that could impact the status quo in the federal arena. History has shown that voters can vote one way at state level and then another at federal elections. But Saturday's poll feels like it will be a watershed in Australian politics and the fallout could have big ramifications.(james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
